facts: Elrod separates two kinds of miracles.
A passive miracle is an event nobody can explain and nobody controls.
The book's example is Donnie Register, who was working in an antique store when he was about to be shot.
He raised his hands to his face, and the bullet bounced off his gold wedding ring.
An active, or created, miracle is one a person makes through belief, determination and hard work.
Elrod says people have more control over created miracles than they think.
He calls people who pursue created miracles instead of waiting for passive ones Miracle Mavens.
Skepticism is reasonable, but it can slide into cynicism, the thought of what is the point.
Setbacks will happen on the way to a created miracle, and Elrod says to treat roadblocks as learning opportunities, not hurdles.
Even if you miss the end goal, he says, you learn something that can lead you down a different road.
scene_details: a gold wedding ring that deflects a bullet
tension: A bullet bouncing off a wedding ring is the kind of miracle no one can plan, and Elrod uses it to show what he does not mean by the word.
opening_idea: Open on the man in the antique store with his hands up at his face and the ring.

lessons.idea: Waiting for luck and building a result are different projects; most of what we call a miracle for others we can only produce ourselves.
lessons.anchor: Passive miracle (the ring) versus created miracle (Miracle Maven).

reflect_final: What is one thing you have been hoping would just work out that you could instead start building, and what would the first move be?

use_cases.situation: A colleague is waiting for a lucky break on a project
use_cases.move: Like Donnie Register's ring, a lucky break cannot be planned. Which part of this can we make happen ourselves this week?

use_cases.situation: A friend says people who succeed just got lucky
use_cases.move: Elrod says passive miracles exist, but you have more control over the created kind. Which kind are you hoping for?

use_cases.situation: You are hoping a hard decision will sort itself out
use_cases.move: Write down one step you could take today that does not depend on luck.

pocket_idea: A miracle that happens to you is luck; a miracle you make is work you can start today.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A bullet bounced off a wedding ring, and Elrod says that is exactly the miracle you should not wait for.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Donnie Register was working in an antique store when someone was about to shoot him. He threw his hands up to his face and the bullet bounced off his gold wedding ring. Hal Elrod calls that a passive miracle: nobody can explain it or plan it. His book is about the other kind, created miracles, which people make through belief and hard work, and he calls the people who go after them Miracle Mavens.
